sources.name: Reinhart and Rogoff (2010)
sources.text: "Growth in a Time of Debt", American Economic Review Papers and Proceedings 100(2), May 2010, pp. 573-78. Cited for publication details only; its findings and figures are quoted here as reproduced in Herndon, Ash and Pollin (2013).

sources.name: Herndon, Ash and Pollin (2013)
sources.text: "Does High Public Debt Consistently Stifle Economic Growth? A Critique of Reinhart and Rogoff", PERI Working Paper 322, 15 April 2013: the quoted 2010 finding on medians and means; the published average of -0.1 above 90% and the published bucket averages charted here (Table 1, from the authors' NBER working paper, Appendix Table 1); the corrected averages of 4.2, 3.1, 3.2 and 2.2 and the 1-at-a-time and combined effects of each error (Table 3); "Some of the errors have strong interactive effects"; HAP's inability to replicate from the public data and receipt of the authors' working spreadsheet; the averaging of lines 30 to 44 instead of 30 to 49, omitting Australia, Austria, Belgium, Canada and Denmark, "selected alphabetically"; the excluded early years for Australia, New Zealand and Canada, and New Zealand's excluded growth rates of 7.7, 11.9, -9.9 and 10.8 percent; New Zealand's single remaining year, 1951, at -7.6 percent, its 14.3 percent weight, and the transcription to -7.9; the UK's 19 years at 2.4 percent; 96 reported, 110 available and 71 used country-years; 76 media features listed on the authors' website and 538 Google Scholar results, both as of 7 April 2013; and the report that the paper is the only evidence cited on debt and growth in Representative Ryan's "Path to Prosperity", with the budget document's words as quoted by HAP. Read as text extracted from the published PDF.

sources.name: Reinhart and Rogoff (2013)
sources.text: "Errata: 'Growth in A Time of Debt'", 5 May 2013: thanks to HAP "for pointing out an important correction"; "the coding error pointed out to us by HAP", which excluded Australia, Austria, Belgium, Canada and Denmark; the added years for Spain; New Zealand's 1948 and 1949 included as "a coding correction", and the replacement of the Maddison GDP series used in the 2010 paper; the final postwar mean above 90% of GDP of 2.0 (NZ Historical Statistics GDP) and 1.0 (Maddison GDP), Table 1; HAP's silence on the longer sample and emerging markets; and the statement that HAP "fails to mention that our median estimates for the postwar sample are very close in magnitude to the averages that they present". Read as text extracted from the published PDF.
